dedupe_keys.name: port statistics from the mlit port survey kowan chosa japan

description: The Port Survey is Japan's only fundamental statistical survey on ports, run by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) to show the actual state of ports for their development, use and management. Its results, the Port Statistics, report ships entering port, maritime cargo loaded and unloaded, container counts and related figures, and are used by port managers for cargo forecasts in port plans, economic analysis of ports and logistics policy. Coverage is national (Japan), by port. The statistics are free to browse and download on e-Stat, the government statistics portal, as annual reports (85 tables, last updated January 2025) and monthly reports (26 tables, last updated September 2026), in CSV and other formats, and through the e-Stat API, which needs a free user registration for an application ID; no licence was read on the day. Caveats: tables follow survey definitions by port class, and older years may be available only as files. They support port demand and capacity planning, supply chain disruption analysis and recovery monitoring after events such as earthquakes and tsunamis. They complement the KSJ port data and are related to the DfT maritime and shipping statistics.
